newsitem.title: CANADA: Quebec says on deficit target track with job cuts.
newsitem.headline: Quebec says on deficit target track with job cuts.

text.p: Quebec said on Thursday it will meet its fiscal 1997/98 budget deficit target of C$2.2 billion, as a greater number than expected of government employees had opted for employment buyout offers.

Quebec Treasury Board President Jacques Leonard told reporters that 24,361 government employees had voluntarily left service since July 1 and 1,000 more departures were expected, representing six per cent of the total government workforce.
Leonard said the departures will reduce its annual payroll costs by more than C$800 million in 1997/98 and C$1.1 billion in 1998/99.
"The government has met its financial objectives and will even surpass them," Leonard said at a news conference.
More than 3,000 young people will be hired to replace some of the departing employees and nearly 7,000 departing teachers and nurses will be replaced, he said.
Quebec's fiscal year ends March 31. In fiscal 1996/97, its budget deficit was C$3.25 billion.
